manual_reviewer_checklist.scope_note: Machine proof for these items is geometric and headless. Only the owner can confirm the live feel (indicator visibility, cursor, drag tracking, recovery on a shrinking window).

items.step: Click the PROJECTS title bar twice (and SNAPS, LAYERS).
items.machine_proven: ToggleCollapsed returns the exact previous state; the documented order is unchanged; P1/P2 pass.
items.human_must_verify: The menu really rolls up to its title bar, the glyph flips, the status line reads 'Projects rolled up' / 'Projects expanded', and the second click restores the body, its scroll and its height.

items.step: Drag the PROJECTS title bar above DISPLAY, release; then drag it to the bottom of the column.
items.machine_proven: Drop index rule, Move saturation, AlreadyThere/no-op reporting, invariant 'each menu exactly once, dense order'.
items.human_must_verify: The 3 px red insertion line follows the pointer, the release reorders the column, and the status line reads 'Projects moved to menu position 3'.

items.step: Drag MAIN MENU into the middle of a viewport, release; then move the floating window and press its X.
items.machine_proven: Float keeps a home, the drop preview rect equals the applied rect, the readback is not reported as recovery, closing restores home and left order.
items.human_must_verify: The float preview frame appears while dragging, the window floats over the model without jumping, and X returns the menu to its old slot with the same roll-up state.

items.step: With the right column hidden, drag a menu into the 48 px strip at the right edge; then press ◀ in the right column. Repeat in a window narrower than 1200 points.
items.machine_proven: Strip = rightmost 48 px of the views; Place{Right} from the strip; Dock restores home with restored_home=true; under 1200 points there is no strip and the drop floats instead.
items.human_must_verify: The right column appears exactly where the strip was offered, the menu is not lost, and below 1200 points nothing docks right (the menu floats).

items.step: Float a menu to the bottom-right corner, then shrink the window until it must move.
items.machine_proven: SetFloatRect clamps into the work area and reports Recovered; resync_floats pulls a stored rectangle back inside; a window below the plan floor changes nothing.
items.human_must_verify: The floating menu is pulled inside and stays usable, the warning names it, and no menu disappears or jumps outside the screen.

items.step: Drag a menu past the right edge of the screen and release; then drag again and press Esc while a command draft is open.
items.machine_proven: FloatOutside adds the OutsideMainWindow note plus recovery; a lost pointer cancels; Escape cancels and does not fall through to the command controller.
items.human_must_verify: The menu lands inside the window with the warning 'cannot float outside the main window', and Esc cancels the drag while the typed draft stays in the command box.

what_it_proves: the preview a pressed drag shows is the operation the release applies (reorder: Place{left,2} + a 3 px line at the DISPLAY bar top; dock-right: Place{right,0} + the 48 px strip at x=1552)
a real drop into a viewport floats the menu and keeps its home (float-drop: floating=[display], home={left,2}, left order loses display)
the roll-up round trip in a real window: 'Projects rolled up' then 'Projects expanded' with the documented order unchanged
a rectangle the real window reports is read back and repaired with the warning 'Display was moved back inside the window' (readback-recover)
Escape cancels a real drag: layout unchanged, status Info 'Display drag cancelled (Esc)'
the work area the application used is [8, 29, 1584, 943] at 1600x1000, as the fixture records
no menu drag touched document entities or the undo journal
limitations: the X of the floating window is not scripted (a 16 px target): closing it is p7 plus the owner's item M3
the window keeps its audit size, so the repair comes from the rectangle the real window reports; the shrinking-window case is the owner's item M5
